 Oral Judgment

This Miscellaneous Second Appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 30.07.2016 passed in RA.No.92/2016 on the file of VI Additional District & Sessions Judge, Tumakuru and the Judgment and award dated 05.11.2011 passed in LAC No.94/2006 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Gubbi, seeking enhancement of compensation praying to award the compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta and Rs.38,250/- per tamarind tree for four tamarind trees.
2.

The claimant's land bearing Sy.No.81/2, measuring 03 acre 17 guntas situated at Nanadihalli Village, NC: 2024:KHC:44944 Gubbi Taluk, Tumakuru District was acquired for the project of formation of the Hemavathi Canal under preliminary notification dated 20.02.1992 and final notification dated 04.03.1993.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) has determined compensation of Rs.590/- per gunta.
The Reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.600/- per gunta and awarded compensation of Rs.8,000/- per tamarind tree for four tamarind trees.

3. Being aggrieved by this, the appellant/claimant has preferred regular appeal before the District Court and the District Court has enhanced compensation by granting Rs.2000/- per gunta and Rs.15,000/- per tamarind tree for four tamarind trees.
4. The appellant/claimant has preferred the present appeal for seeking further enhancement of compensation on the reason that in the very same village for the very same project the neighboring Sri Panchakasharaiah vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183818503/

sentences.text: 2 land owners have been awarded the compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta and Rs.38,250/- per tamarind tree.

Therefore, on this line prays for enhancement of compensation by placing reliance on the NC: 2024:KHC:44944 judgment of this Court in the case of Smt. Shivamma & others Vs. The Special Land Acquisition Officer in MSA No.135/2021 (LAC) dated 06.02.2023 (Shivamma's Case).
5.

entities.text: Smt. Shivamma & others Vs. The Special Land Acquisition Officer in MSA No.135/2021 (LAC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Additional Government Advocate and also learned counsel Sri. K.S. Bheemaiah,
appearing for the beneficiary justified the order and award passed by the District Court and prays to confirm the same by dismissing the appeal.

6. This Court in Shivamma's Case (supra) has awarded a compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta, by observing that in the very same village the lands acquired for the very same project, the District Court has granted a compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta and accordingly accepting the same, the claimants in that case were also situated on the same pedestal.
Accordingly, granted compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Union of India Vs. Balaram and another reported in AIR 2004 SC 3981, has held that it is not fair to make discrimination NC: 2024:KHC:44944 between the land owners for granting compensation when the purpose of acquisition is for the same project and the lands are identical in nature.

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Balaram and another reported in AIR 2004 SC 3981
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Therefore, this Court in Shivamma's Case (supra) the claimants were awarded compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
In this case also the claimant's lands situated in the same Nandahalli Village of Gubbi Taluk, Tumakuru District.
Therefore, there could not be any discrimination between the agriculturists, who have lost their land due to acquisition.
Therefore, on the parity in the present case also, the appellant/claimant is entitled compensation of Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
Accordingly, it is awarded.
9. The Reference Court has awarded a sum of Rs.600/- per gunta and Rs.8,000/- per tamarind tree.
The same was enhanced by District Court at Rs.2,000/- per gunta and Rs.15,000/- per tamarind tree.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant prays that the District Court, Tumkur, in other cases for the very same village for one tamarind tree a sum of Rs.38,250/- was awarded.

Hence, NC:
2024:KHC:44944 prays to grant compensation on this parity.

This is vehemently opposed by the learned counsel for respondent No.2/beneficiary and submitted that the compensation is determined for tamarind tree depends upon the age of the tree, yield per quintal and nature of soil,
etc., but there is no evidence by the appellant/claimant in this regard.
Hence, justified the compensation granted for tamarind tree by the District Court is correct.
The Reference Court and District Court have referred that the tamarind tree is a big tree.
In absence of evidence regarding what would be the average yield of one tamarind tree and age of tamarind tree is to be made through guesswork.
When the tamarind tree is found to be big in nature, considering the tamarind is a commercial crop therefore, at least one tamarind tree will fetch revenue of Rs.38,000/-.

When a similarly situated agriculturist received a compensation of Rs.38,250/- per tamarind tree, the appellant/claimant shall not be discriminated in this regard, when the land is situated in the same place as that of other land losers.

Therefore, in Manjunathiah Vs. The Special Land Acquisition Officer passed in NC: 2024:KHC:44944 R.A.No.193/2018 dated 15.07.2019 on the file IV Additional Sri Panchakasharaiah vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183818503/

10. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The market value of the subject land is fixed at Rs.6,000/- per gunta.
iii. A compensation of Rs.38,250/- per tamarind tree for four tamarind trees is awarded.
iv. The appellant/claimant is entitled all admissible and statutory benefits including interest and costs.
v. The claimant is not entitled interest for the delayed period of 1601 days in filing the appeal.

vi. It is hereby directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of NC:
2024:KHC:44944 six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
vii. The deficit Court fee to be made good, if any, at the time drawing up of award.
